algebra.notation: K is exact known_hosts bytes; N_Q(C) decodes and splitlines the config, rewrites every recognized UserKnownHostsFile line to Q, joins LF and appends LF; G builds the exact canonical profile from new paths, output content hashes, current binary hashes, current agent and current socket parent.
conditions: P1 and P2 are the fixed direct paths without whitespace or line separators; the input replacement path remains one token.
P2 is a fresh output in either hypothetical execution.
E2 supplies the same current executable file contents and socket-parent identity; A2 is the same current agent.
Existing config/known bytes are unchanged and match the explicitly bound private seed.
reasoning: After first generation all original line separators have become LF and rewriting again is idempotent.
The first generated profile names Q1, and every rewritten directive also names Q1, so the second invocation checks and replaces the same directives with Q2.
Non-target config lines and known_hosts bytes are identical along both successful paths.
All final profile fields are constants, P2-derived paths/content hashes, or currently re-read E2 binaries and A2/socket arguments; no first generation executable hash or agent is reused.
limitations: The full return receipt is not equal: template_sha256 records the actual seed body, hence fe1e versus ed680 differs.
Fresh file inode/time metadata is outside the content equality claim.
This does not prove arbitrary path/token inputs, partial failure paths, or byte identity of the old missing836-byte seed.
The existing topology guard must truthfully bind the new seed SHA; the original796-byte topology is retained, and only its64-byte profile hash value is replaced in a new file.
